rationale.a: Isolator 500 N/unit, attach to roof membrane with stainless steel straps; coastal salt-spray requires marine-grade coatings only.
rationale.b: Isolator 2,000 N/unit (overly conservative), attach to flexible roof frames to absorb wind vibration.

rationale.correct: Step 1: Equipment weight force = 80 kg × 9.81 m/s² = 785 N. Step 2: Vibration isolator rating (1.5× margin) = 785 N × 1.5 = 1,177 N ≈ 1,200 N minimum per unit. For 4 units per floor = 4 × 1,200 N = 4,800 N total isolator capacity required. Step 3: Structural attachment per PD 1058 Section 5.3: Mount to building frame (not roof membrane alone) using anchor bolts or structural steel bracing to columns/beams. Typhoon Category 5 (200 km/h) requires rigid tie-down; roof-only mounting risks uplift and cascading unit failure. Source: PD 1058 Section 5.3; ALE-UTIL-002-04 Tropical Climate Considerations Outdoor Unit Placement.
rationale.takeaway: Typhoon-resilient outdoor unit bracing requires: (1) vibration isolators rated ≥1.5× equipment weight, (2) attachment to building structural frame (not roof membrane), (3) stainless steel fasteners in coastal salt-spray zones per ASHRAE durability standards.
